title: run.jl: entry point glue script
description: Create run.jl: the main entry point runnable via 'julia run.jl'. (1) Include all source files in dependency order: config.jl, tensor_ops.jl, attention.jl, model.jl, data.jl, train.jl, generate.jl. (2) Download and prepare Shakespeare data. (3) Build vocab, create batches, train/val split. (4) Initialize GPT model with default config. (5) Run training loop. (6) Generate sample text (500 chars) with temperature=0.8 and print. (7) Print final train/val loss summary. ~50 LOC.

title: generate.jl: autoregressive text generation
description: Create generate.jl: (1) generate(model, context, max_new_tokens; temperature=1.0, top_k=0) -> token_ids: autoregressive generation. Feed context, take logits at last position, apply temperature scaling (logits/T), optionally apply top-k (zero out all but top k logits), softmax, sample (or argmax if temperature=0). Append token, repeat. Forward pass only, no backward. (2) sample_token(logits; temperature, top_k): single-token sampling helper. (3) Handle context longer than seq_len by truncating to last seq_len tokens. ~70 LOC.

title: attention.jl: linear projections and causal mask
description: Create attention.jl. Implement: (1) AttentionParams struct holding Wq, Wk, Wv, Wo matrices (D,D each) and biases. (2) linear_forward(W, b, x) -> (y, cache): y=W*x+b for each (t,b) slice. Cache stores (W, b, x). (3) linear_backward(cache, grad_y) -> (grad_x, grad_W, grad_b): dL/dW = grad_y*x^T summed over T,B; dL/dx = W^T*grad_y. Include matmul gradient derivation. (4) causal_mask(T) -> upper-triangular mask of -Inf. ~80 LOC.

title: tests.jl: test harness and Tier 1 tests (stubs)
description: Create tests.jl with a minimal test harness (no Test stdlib). Implement: (1) check(name, condition) function that prints PASS/FAIL with colors and accumulates results. (2) run_all_tests() entry point. (3) Tier 1 test stubs for tensor_ops: softmax forward (sums to 1, positive, shift-invariant), softmax backward gradcheck, layer_norm forward (mean≈0, var≈1), layer_norm backward gradcheck, relu forward, relu backward gradcheck, cross_entropy forward (uniform and perfect cases), cross_entropy backward gradcheck. Tests should fail initially (TDD red phase). ~80 LOC.

title: train.jl: training loop with eval
description: Add to train.jl: (1) train_epoch!(model, batches, config, step) -> (avg_loss, step): iterate over batches, forward, backward, clip gradients, SGD step, accumulate loss. (2) evaluate(model, batches) -> avg_loss: forward-only over val batches. (3) train!(model, train_batches, val_batches, config): outer loop over n_epochs calling train_epoch! and evaluate. Print train/val loss each epoch. Track best val loss. Return training history for inspection. ~80 LOC.

title: model.jl: full GPT model forward/backward
description: Add to model.jl: (1) GPT struct holding token embedding E_tok (D,V), list of TransformerBlocks, final LayerNorm, and output projection W_out (V,D). (2) init_gpt(config) -> GPT: initialize all weights using Xavier/GPT-2 init. (3) gpt_forward(model, token_ids) -> (logits, cache): embed tokens, add sinusoidal PE, run through n_layers transformer blocks, final layer norm, project to vocab. logits shape (V,T,B). (4) gpt_backward(model, cache, grad_logits) -> grads dict: backprop through entire model collecting all parameter gradients. ~100 LOC.

title: tensor_ops.jl: layer_norm forward and backward
description: Add to tensor_ops.jl: (1) layer_norm_forward(x, gamma, beta; eps=1e-5) -> (y, cache): normalize along dim 1 (feature dim). Cache stores (x, x_hat, gamma, mu, sigma_inv). (2) layer_norm_backward(cache, grad_y) -> (grad_x, grad_gamma, grad_beta): full backward with dL/dsigma^2 and dL/dmu terms. Include complete derivation in block comment showing all intermediate gradient steps in index notation. Array shape: (D, T, B). Must pass Tier 1 layer_norm tests. ~70 LOC.

title: tensor_ops.jl: weight initialization utilities
description: Add to tensor_ops.jl: (1) xavier_init(fan_in, fan_out) -> W: W ~ Normal(0, sqrt(2/(fan_in+fan_out))). (2) gpt2_init(fan_in, fan_out; scale=1.0) -> W: W ~ Normal(0, 0.02*scale). Include block comment deriving Var[y]=n*Var[w]*Var[x] and why Xavier keeps variance stable. (3) zeros_init(dims...) for biases. These are pure utility functions, no backward needed. ~40 LOC.

title: tensor_ops.jl: embedding and sinusoidal positional encoding
description: Add to tensor_ops.jl: (1) embed_forward(E, token_ids) -> (h, cache): lookup rows from embedding matrix E (D,V). token_ids is (T,B) of integers. Output (D,T,B). Cache stores (E, token_ids). (2) embed_backward(cache, grad_h) -> grad_E: scatter-add into embedding gradient matrix. (3) sinusoidal_pe(seq_len, d_model) -> PE matrix (D,T): Vaswani formula with sin for even dims, cos for odd dims. PE is constant (no learnable params, no gradient). ~60 LOC.

title: gradcheck.jl: finite-difference gradient verification
description: Create gradcheck.jl with standalone finite-difference gradient checking utilities. Implement: (1) numerical_gradient(f, x, eps=1e-5) that computes (f(x+eps*e_i) - f(x-eps*e_i))/(2*eps) for each element. (2) check_gradient(f_forward, f_backward, x; eps=1e-5, tol=1e-5) that compares analytical vs numerical gradients and returns max relative error. (3) Helper to handle multi-argument functions (perturb one arg at a time). Works on Array{Float64}. No dependencies beyond LinearAlgebra. ~60 LOC.

title: train.jl: SGD optimizer, LR schedule, gradient clipping
description: Create train.jl: (1) sgd_step!(params, grads, lr): theta <- theta - lr * grad for each parameter. In-place update. (2) lr_schedule(step, config) -> lr: linear warmup over warmup_steps then cosine decay. Formula: eta(t)=eta_max*(t/warmup_steps) if t<warmup_steps, else eta_min+0.5*(eta_max-eta_min)*(1+cos(pi*progress)). (3) clip_gradients!(grads, max_norm) -> clipped_grads: global norm clipping g <- g*min(1, c/||g||_2). (4) collect_all_params(model) and collect_all_grads(model, grad_dict): flatten param/grad access. ~70 LOC.

title: tests.jl: Tier 4 data pipeline tests
description: Add Tier 4 tests to tests.jl: (1) Tokenization round-trip: encode then decode recovers original string. (2) Batch shapes: input is (T,B) integers in [1,V], target is same shape. (3) No off-by-one: target[t] == input[t+1] for sequential text. (4) Train/val split: val data starts exactly where train data ends, no overlap. Use a small synthetic string for testing (avoid downloading Shakespeare in tests). Tests fail initially (TDD red phase). ~60 LOC.

title: model.jl: transformer block forward/backward
description: Create model.jl. Implement: (1) TransformerBlock struct holding attention params, FFN weights (W1 (d_ff,D), b1, W2 (D,d_ff), b2), and two LayerNorm param sets (gamma, beta). (2) transformer_block_forward(block, h) -> (out, cache): pre-norm residual pattern: h + MHA(LN(h)), then h + FFN(ReLU(LN(h))). Cache all intermediates. (3) transformer_block_backward(cache, grad_out) -> (grad_h, grads...): backprop through residuals, layer norms, attention, FFN. Residual gradient flows through unchanged. ~100 LOC.

title: tensor_ops.jl: relu and cross_entropy forward/backward
description: Add to tensor_ops.jl: (1) relu_forward(x) -> (y, cache): y = max.(0, x), cache stores mask. (2) relu_backward(cache, grad_y) -> grad_x: grad_y .* mask. (3) cross_entropy_forward(logits, targets) -> (loss, cache): fused softmax + cross-entropy. logits shape (V, T, B), targets (T, B) integers. Returns scalar mean loss. Cache stores (probs, targets). (4) cross_entropy_backward(cache) -> grad_logits: probs - one_hot(target), divided by (T*B). Include derivation comments. Must pass Tier 1 relu and cross_entropy tests. ~80 LOC.

title: tensor_ops.jl: softmax forward and backward
description: Implement in tensor_ops.jl: (1) softmax_forward(x) -> (s, cache): numerically stable softmax (subtract max), operates along dim 1. Returns probabilities and cache=(s,). (2) softmax_backward(cache, grad_s) -> grad_x: using dL/dx_i = s_i*(dL/ds_i - sum_j s_j*dL/ds_j). Include full derivation in block comment with index notation. Array layout: features along first dimension. Must pass Tier 1 softmax tests. ~50 LOC.

title: config.jl: GPTConfig struct and defaults
description: Create config.jl with the GPTConfig struct holding all model hyperparameters. Fields: vocab_size (65), d_model (128), n_heads (4), n_layers (4), seq_len (256), d_ff (512). Include a default constructor and a convenience constructor that computes d_ff=4*d_model. Also define TrainConfig struct with batch_size (32), learning_rate (1e-3), warmup_steps (100), n_epochs (20), max_grad_norm (1.0). ~50 LOC.

title: tests.jl: Tier 5 training loop tests
description: Add Tier 5 tests to tests.jl: (1) Single SGD step decreases loss on a fixed batch -- if not, LR or gradients are wrong. (2) LR schedule: warmup is linear, value at t=0 is 0 (or eta_min), value at t=warmup_steps is eta_max. Cosine decay reaches eta_min at end. (3) Gradient clipping: after clipping, ||g||_2 <= max_grad_norm + epsilon. Use a small model (D=16, 1 layer) for the SGD test. Tests fail initially (TDD red phase). ~60 LOC.

title: tests.jl: Tier 3 model tests
description: Add Tier 3 tests to tests.jl: (1) Single transformer block: forward produces correct output shape (D,T,B), backward produces gradients for all parameters. (2) Full model forward: logits shape is (V,T,B). (3) Full model backward: every parameter tensor has a corresponding gradient of the same shape. (4) Overfit test: 2-layer model with D=32 on 4 sequences must drive loss below 0.1 within 200 SGD steps. This is the most critical test -- if it fails, there is a backward pass bug. Tests fail initially (TDD red phase). ~80 LOC.

title: tests.jl: Tier 6 generation tests
description: Add Tier 6 tests to tests.jl: (1) Greedy on a trained model is deterministic (same seed, same output). (2) Temperature=0 matches greedy. (3) Top-k with k=1 matches greedy. (4) Output length matches requested max_new_tokens. Use a tiny model (D=16, 1 layer, V=10) with random weights -- correctness of text doesn't matter, only behavioral properties. Tests fail initially (TDD red phase). ~50 LOC.

title: attention.jl: single-head and multi-head causal attention
description: Add to attention.jl: (1) single_head_attention_forward(Q, K, V, mask) -> (out, cache): scores = Q^T K / sqrt(Dh), apply mask, softmax, multiply by V. (2) single_head_attention_backward(cache, grad_out) -> (grad_Q, grad_K, grad_V): backprop through softmax and scaled dot-product. (3) multi_head_attention_forward(params, x) -> (out, cache): split into H heads, project Q/K/V, run attention per head, concat, project output Wo. (4) multi_head_attention_backward(cache, grad_out) -> (grad_x, grads...): chain rule through all projections. Full derivation comments. ~100 LOC.

title: tests.jl: Tier 2 attention tests
description: Add Tier 2 tests to tests.jl: (1) Single-head attention on identity-like inputs: when Q=K, attention weights should be uniform-ish. (2) Causal mask: verify attention weights are zero above the diagonal. (3) Multi-head output shape is (D,T,B) regardless of n_heads; n_heads=1 matches single-head. (4) Forward-backward round trip: gradcheck on Q,K,V projection weights with small inputs (D=8, T=4, H=2, B=2). Tests fail initially (TDD red phase). ~80 LOC.

title: data.jl: download, tokenize, and batch Shakespeare
description: Create data.jl: (1) download_shakespeare(path) -> downloads from Karpathy's char-rnn URL if file not present. (2) build_vocab(text) -> (char_to_idx, idx_to_char): character-level vocab from unique sorted chars. 1-indexed for Julia. (3) encode(text, char_to_idx) / decode(ids, idx_to_char): tokenization round-trip. (4) make_batches(data, seq_len, batch_size) -> Vector of (input, target) tuples: non-overlapping windows of seq_len+1, input/target offset by 1, grouped into batches. (5) train_val_split(data; split=0.9): sequential 90/10 split. ~80 LOC.
